text:
# Compositing and Blending

Also called: Accumulate, Alternative Compositing Schemes, Blending Modes, First Hit, Front-to-back blending, Maximum Intensity blending, Minimum Intensity blending

## Overview
Compositing and Blending defines the mathematical and algorithmic rules for combining volumetric samples $(c_i, \alpha_i)$ along a ray into a final pixel color. It solves the problem of optical integration, determining how emitted and scattered light from volume elements is attenuated by absorption and combined with background light. It sets itself apart from [Projection and MIP Techniques](6305-projection-and-mip-techniques.md) by explicitly modeling opacity and transmittance for depth-aware blending, and from [Volume Raycasting Output Generation](4277-volume-raycasting-output-generation.md) by focusing on the specific accumulation logic rather than the broader output pipeline.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a sequence of samples $(c_i, \alpha_i)$ encountered along a ray, where $c_i$ is the sample color (RGB) and $\alpha_i$ is the sample opacity (A) [S1, S2, unofficial]. The core mechanism involves an accumulator state $(C_{acc}, \alpha_{acc})$ initialized to $(0, 0)$ (or background color/opacity) and updated iteratively for each sample [S1, S2, unofficial].

The standard optical model assumes that light is emitted or scattered by the volume and attenuated by absorption [S1, unofficial]. The [standard front-to-back compositing](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) equation updates these accumulators for each sample $i$ from front to back:
$$
C_{acc}^{(i)} = C_{acc}^{(i-1)} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)}) \alpha_i C_i
$$
$$
\alpha_{acc}^{(i)} = \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)}) \alpha_i
$$
where $C_{acc}^{(0)} = 0$ and $\alpha_{acc}^{(0)} = 0$ [S12, S43, S50]. The term $(1 - \alpha_{acc}^{(i-1)})$ represents the transmittance, i.e., the fraction of light reaching sample $i$ from the camera side [S1, S51].

In iterative form using transmittance $T = 1 - \alpha_{acc}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{final} &\leftarrow C_{final} + c_i \cdot \alpha_i \cdot T \\
T &\leftarrow T \cdot (1 - \alpha_i)
\end{aligned}
$$
Where $T$ is initialized to $1.0$ and represents the accumulated transparency $\prod (1-\alpha_j)$ [G].

The final pixel color is often composited over a background color $C_{bg}$ using $C_{final} = C_{acc} + (1 - \alpha_{acc}) C_{bg}$ [S1, S14].

Early ray termination is a common optimization where the loop breaks if $\alpha_{acc}$ exceeds a threshold (e.g., 1.0), as further samples contribute negligibly to the color [S10, S12].

## Subtopics

### [Pre-Integration Lookup](2854-pre-integration-lookup.md)
[Pre-Integration Lookup](2854-pre-integration-lookup.md) replaces iterative accumulation with a single texture fetch from a pre-computed table, solving the performance bottleneck of evaluating the optical integration equation for every sample. It assumes linear data evolution within a slab, allowing the final color and opacity contribution to be determined solely by entry density, exit density, and thickness. Choose it when performance is critical and transfer functions allow for [slab-based approximation](#1449-projected-slabs-approximation.md).

### [Binary Swap Compositing](3264-binary-swap-compositing.md)
[Binary Swap Compositing](3264-binary-swap-compositing.md) is a parallel image merging algorithm that combines independently rendered sub-images from multiple processors into a final volume-rendered image. It solves the bottleneck of naive binary [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) by ensuring every processor participates in every stage of the merge via a binary-swap tree structure. Choose it for distributed rendering environments where load balancing and communication overhead are concerns.

### [Screen-space Post-processing](3621-screen-space-post-processing.md)
[Screen-space Post-processing](3621-screen-space-post-processing.md) applies aspect-ratio preserving UV covering, luminance-based bright passes, color grading, and spatial effects ([bloom](#4906-bloom.md), blur, vignetting) to a scene texture. It differs from ray-casting compositing by operating entirely in screen space on the final 2D image, allowing for complex aesthetic effects like underwater refraction without modifying the [volume rendering pipeline](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md). Choose it for final image enhancement and aesthetic control.

### [Layered SDF Compositing](3641-layered-sdf-compositing.md)
[Layered SDF Compositing](3641-layered-sdf-compositing.md) renders Signed Distance Field ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) glyphs by compositing multiple layers (face and outline layers) using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) and pre-multiplied alpha handling. It operates on discrete, pre-sampled layers of a 2D texture atlas rather than continuous 3D volume data, allowing for efficient, sharp text rendering. Choose it for SDF-based text or glyph rendering.

### [Reconstruction and Compositing Techniques](4646-reconstruction-and-compositing-techniques.md)
[Reconstruction and Compositing Techniques](4646-reconstruction-and-compositing-techniques.md) encompasses the mathematical methods for transforming discrete volumetric data into continuous signals and combining them into final pixel colors. It focuses on the underlying signal processing (reconstruction) and the specific mathematical formulation of the accumulation, ranging from [standard alpha blending](#5697-hardware-alpha-blending-compositing.md) to differentiable training passes. Choose it when precise signal reconstruction or differentiable rendering is required.

### [Lighting-Specific Compositing](5940-lighting-specific-compositing.md)
[Lighting-Specific Compositing](5940-lighting-specific-compositing.md) modifies the standard front-to-back compositing equation to incorporate complex lighting effects (in-scattering, multi-channel illumination, [Phong shading](#1853-phong-shading.md)) directly into the accumulation step. It computes lighting contributions per sample before blending. Choose it when accurate illumination within the volume is required beyond simple emission/absorption.

### [Layer-Centric Volume Rendering Framework](6994-layer-centric-volume-rendering-framework.md)
[Layer-Centric Volume Rendering Framework](6994-layer-centric-volume-rendering-framework.md) decomposes volume visualization into rendering small regions of interest (ROIs) as separate [layers and compositing](#4539-multi-layer-surface-compositing.md) them using a rich set of 2D operators. It treats the final image as a composition of independent renderings, allowing for intuitive 2D-based user interactions. Choose it for interactive applications requiring complex material manipulations and layer-based editing.

### [MAB Compositing with Gaze-Contingent Blending](8211-mab-compositing-with-gaze-contingent-blending.md)
[MAB Compositing with Gaze-Contingent Blending](8211-mab-compositing-with-gaze-contingent-blending.md) maps framebuffer fragments to a Multi-Anchor Buffer ([MAB](#8219-multiresolution-atlas-buffer-mab.md)) to retrieve and blend color values from different resolution levels based on gaze distance. It solves the problem of maintaining high frame rates in VR by dynamically adjusting rendering resolution. Choose it for immersive VR applications where performance fluctuation causes cybersickness.

### [Multi-view image blending](9831-multi-view-image-blending.md)
[Multi-view image blending](9831-multi-view-image-blending.md) reduces view-dependent artifacts (ghosting, transparency variation) by combining multiple pre-rendered images from different camera angles. It selects and blends at least three textures to approximate volumetric appearance. Choose it for static or slow-moving scenes where high-quality view-dependent effects are needed and memory bandwidth allows.

### [Dynamic Job-Scheduling for Grid Volume Rendering](10585-dynamic-job-scheduling-for-grid-volume-rendering.md)
[Dynamic Job-Scheduling for Grid Volume Rendering](10585-dynamic-job-scheduling-for-grid-volume-rendering.md) is a distributed rendering strategy that dynamically determines the processing order of sub-volumes based on visibility using [obstacle-flags](#14294-obstacle-flag.md). It avoids bottlenecks of static sequential scheduling by dispatching jobs as soon as they become combinable. Choose it for large-scale grid computing environments with heterogeneous agent speeds.

### [HardSoftRas Blending](10747-hardsoftras-blending.md)
[HardSoftRas Blending](10747-hardsoftras-blending.md) is a pixel-wise compositing strategy for differentiable rendering that distinguishes between edge pixels and non-edge pixels to balance anti-aliasing with texture sharpness. It preserves frontal color for non-edge regions while using probabilistic blending for edges. Choose it for differentiable rendering pipelines requiring sharp internal textures and far-range gradients.

### Commutative Blend Direct Volume Rendering
A rendering technique for unsorted [cell projection](#26-cell-projection.md) using [optical models](#33-optical-models.md) that lead to a commutative blend function, allowing compositing in arbitrary order [S3]. It applies arbitrary transfer functions via texture lookup, which only affect the generation of the texture map [S3]. Models allowing arbitrary order compositing include maximum intensity projection and restrictions of the full volume density model to either the source term or the absorption term [S3].

### Frame Buffer Copy / Blit
A pass that simply copies the current frame to the output, acting as a simple integration or blit step for the [LAO](#4502-local-ambient-occlusion-lao.md) renderer [S4, unofficial]. It samples the frame buffer: `oColor = texture(uFrame, vPosition);` [S4, unofficial].

### Virtual Dimension Expansion for Compositing
A post-processing step where partial images rendered from blocks of different resolutions are expanded to a common 'virtual dimension' (the highest resolution dimension of the block) before compositing [S5, unofficial]. This allows standard compositing algorithms to work despite varying input resolutions [S5, unofficial]. The virtual dimension can be set to the dimension of the largest subimage in the scene to minimize padding, or fixed to the global high-resolution block size [S5, unofficial].

### Voronoi Painter's Algorithm Compositing
A rendering compositing strategy where the scene is rendered part-by-part (one Voronoi cell at a time) and the resulting cell images are composited back-to-front to generate the final image [S6]. It relies on the proof that Voronoi cells admit a partial ordering compatible with occlusion [S6]. The ordering is defined as $V_{P'} <_Q V_P$ if and only if $d(P', Q) < d(P, Q)$ [S6]. Standard [Painter's Algorithm](#12692-back-to-front-rendering.md) fails on cyclic occlusion graphs, but Voronoi Painter's is always compatible because the distance-to-camera ordering is a strict partial order [S6].

### Hybrid Compositing (Radix-k)
Hybrid methods like Radix-k combine [direct send](#9377-direct-send-compositing.md) and binary swap approaches depending on the problem setting, adaptively running one or the other based on criteria [S7, unofficial].

### Fabric Compositing
A compositing pass that creates an initial fabric-like texture by combining advected noise fields, silhouette data, and lighting [S8, book]. Pixels not part of the geometry are discarded using the depth buffer [S8, book]. The color channels after $k$ iterations are defined as:
$$
R(x,y) = \frac{r \cdot f_{\lambda_2}(x,y)}{8 \cdot f_{\lambda_1}^2(x,y)} + e_{x,y} + \text{light}(\mathcal{L}_{x,y})
$$
$$
G(x,y) = \frac{(1-r) \cdot f_{\lambda_1}(x,y)}{8 \cdot f_{\lambda_2}^2(x,y)} + e_{x,y} + \text{light}(\mathcal{L}_{x,y})
$$
$$
B(x,y) = e_{x,y} + \text{light}(\mathcal{L}_{x,y})
$$
where $f_{\lambda_1}$ and $f_{\lambda_2}$ are the advected fields, $e_{x,y}$ is the silhouette image, and $r$ blends between tensor directions [S8, book]. Squaring the denominator emphasizes differences [S8, book]. A separate lighting function manipulates intensity without affecting the base color [S8, book].

## Background
The standard front-to-back compositing equation is derived from the [volume rendering integral](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md), assuming emission and absorption [S1, S12, S43, S50]. Early systems like VolumePro supported front-to-back blending, minimum intensity, and maximum intensity blending modes [S1, unofficial]. Accumulate is the [standard volume rendering](#1165-standard-volume-rendering-equation.md) compositing scheme [S2, unofficial]. First Hit renders an isosurface by taking the first sample that exceeds a threshold [S2, unofficial]. Averaging produces X-ray-like images by averaging samples along the ray [S2, unofficial]. [Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP)](#10702-maximum-intensity-projection-mip.md) is often used to extract vessel structures in magnetic resonance angiograms [S2, unofficial].
